entries.name: Field electrification and grid or power-from-shore connection of platforms
entries.summary: Platform gas turbines and diesel generators are replaced by power cables from shore or a regional grid, often with a central field substation, which cuts combustion CO2 and fuel use.

operating_window.scale: Johan Sverdrup: 100 MW phase 1 plus 200 MW phase 2 = 300 MW via ~200 km HVDC cable (Equinor; NKT award)
operating_window.intensity: 0.67 kg CO2/bbl at Johan Sverdrup vs world average ~15 kg (Equinor)
operating_window.cost_drivers: AC vs DC, power demand and distance to shore are the main cost drivers (Norwegian Petroleum Directorate abatement-cost work)
operating_window.other: Depends on a reliable, adequate onshore grid; benefit depends on grid carbon intensity.

entries.capex: Johan Sverdrup phase 1 power supply ~NOK 6 billion (2015 value), reported as ~US$850 million; phase 2 cables just over NOK 1 billion (NKT award, 2018).

evidence.claim: Power from shore gives Johan Sverdrup 0.67 kg CO2 per barrel, under 5% of the ~15 kg world average, avoiding more than 620,000 t CO2/yr.

Norwegian authority review: electrification projects had a measure cost below NOK 1,500 per tonne CO2; Norwegian shelf emissions fell 2.9 Mt CO2e from 2019 to 2024 as CO2 costs rose from ~NOK 860 to 1,860/t.

providers.name: Wolong - ATB Group / Wolong EMEA (Germany) GmbH

reference_fit.reason: Lake platforms are close to shore, but connecting them to the failing Zulia grid would import its blackouts, so this only fits with a dedicated, reliable field power plant.

entries.rationale: Large, well-documented emission cuts at very high capex. The evidence is North Sea operator and authority data, with no refereed study captured.
entries.caveats: Figures are from search snippets. The NOK 1,500/t and the 2.9 Mt figures may come from different Sodir report editions (2020 and newer). The Sodir page returned 403 on fetch. NOK 6bn and US$850M are reported equivalents. Siemens Energy, Nexans and Prysmian are named from general knowledge. Shallow lake platforms would need much shorter AC links. No lake-scale cost data.

entries.name: Variable speed drives and power-quality equipment for field loads
entries.summary: VSDs on ESPs, rod pumps and compressors match motor speed to the well and cut energy use and mechanical stress, while harmonic filters or active-front-end drives keep the power system within IEEE 519 limits.

operating_window.rod_pump_savings: Software frequency-elastic drive mode: up to ~5% energy saving and up to 3% peak polished-rod load reduction, best at 7-10 strokes/min (Montanuniversität Leoben, 2021)
operating_window.esp_savings: ~20% energy saving (19.5 A reduction) in a single-well ESP drive trial (CCW Energy Systems, Oilfield Technology 2013)
operating_window.harmonics: Many field harmonic filters underperformed through wrong sizing, wiring or failed components; AFE drives are less effective on poor-quality supplies (ChampionX, SWPSC 2021)
operating_window.other: Requires electric power at the well.

evidence.claim: Frequency-elastic VSD drive mode on a sucker-rod pump achieved up to ~5% energy saving and up to 3% lower peak polished-rod load.
Oil-field ESP retrofit to meet IEEE 519 harmonic limits at the point of common coupling after complaints from neighbouring utility customers.
evidence.who: Farbis, Hoevenaars & Greenwald, IEEE Trans. Industry Applications 2016

evidence.claim: CCW reports its ESP drive cut running current by 19.5 A (~20% energy saving) while production rose in a field trial.
evidence.who: CCW Energy Systems, via Oilfield Technology

providers.name: Aries Oil Field Services L L C

reference_fit.reason: Helps ESP and rod-pump wells ride through Zulia's poor power quality and cut fuel or grid demand, but brings no benefit to the dominant gas-lift wells and needs power at the well.

entries.rationale: Routine technology with modest, single-study energy savings (5-20%) and no captured cost data.
entries.caveats: Savings figures come from abstracts or trade press, one study each. SPOC's 10-40% (average 20%) claim is marketing and was excluded. No VSD capex/opex source was captured. ABB, Schneider, SLB and Baker Hughes are named from general knowledge. The harmonics findings come from abstracts only.

entries.name: Small-scale associated gas monetisation (mobile CNG, mini/micro-LNG, mini-GTL)
entries.summary: Modular skids compress, liquefy or convert small or stranded associated-gas streams into CNG, LNG or synthetic liquids for trucking or local use, instead of flaring.

operating_window.mini_GTL_range: Plants now span ~100 Mscf/d to 25 MMscf/d (World Bank GGFR mini-GTL bulletin, Feb 2017); earlier Fleisch study sweet spot ~15 MMscf/d
operating_window.CNG_vs_LNG: World Bank/Tractebel compared mini-LNG and CNG for 1-15 MMscf/d; key cost drivers are gas volume and transport distance
operating_window.GTL_yield: INFRA M100: 1 MMscf/d to 100 bbl/d liquids (GGFR 2017)
operating_window.other: Needs a nearby market or road and marine logistics; liquids-rich gas may need NGL removal.

entries.capex: Mini-GTL: ~US$100,000 per daily barrel; INFRA M100 (1 MMscf/d, 100 bbl/d) under US$10 million (World Bank GGFR bulletin, 2017 USD). Earlier estimate ~US$80,000/daily bbl, 5 MMscf/d plant ~US$40M ±50% (Fleisch, c.2012). Mobile CNG: Statoil Bakken system US$1.6 million (2014).
entries.opex: Mini-GTL operating cost excluding feed gas claimed below US$10/bbl (INFRA, via GGFR 2017 bulletin; vendor claim).

evidence.claim: Statoil's Bakken mobile CNG pilot (with GE/Ferus) saved US$2 million in diesel by end-2014, recovering its US$1.6 million investment, by fuelling rigs and frac fleets with wellsite gas.
GGFR reports mini-GTL plants now cover ~100 Mscf/d to 25 MMscf/d, with a 300 Mscf/d GasTechno unit in commercial-site testing and a 1 MMscf/d INFRA demonstration plant at under US$10M.

reference_fit.reason: Could monetise flared gas at stranded Bolívar Coast and lake sites, but local fuel markets, logistics and finance in Venezuela are uncertain, and putting gas into gas lift or power is usually simpler.

entries.name: Emissions monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV) software and measurement-reconciled inventories
entries.summary: Software combines engineering calculations, device inventories and site, aerial or satellite measurements into reconciled, auditable methane and CO2 inventories (for example OGMP 2.0 Level 4/5), and ranks sites for repair.

operating_window.standard: OGMP 2.0 Level 5 requires reconciling site-level measurements with a source-level Level 4 inventory (OGMP Partnership guidance, 2026)
operating_window.gap_closed: Measurement-based estimates ran ~60% above the US EPA inventory (Alvarez et al., Science 2018) and ~3x it (Sherwin et al., Nature 2024)
operating_window.other: Value depends on the quality of measurement inputs (EP01-EP03). Software alone does not reduce emissions.

evidence.claim: Facility-scale measurements gave US oil and gas supply-chain methane of 13±2 Tg/yr (2.3% of gas production), ~60% above the EPA inventory, mainly from abnormal operating conditions that inventories miss.
Aerial measurement inventories for six US regions found losses of 0.75-9.63% of gas production (2.95% weighted), ~3x the government inventory, worth ~US$1 billion/yr in lost gas.
OGMP 2.0 defines Level 5 as reconciliation of site-level measurements with a Level 4 source-level inventory, which sets the reporting requirement MRV software must support.

reference_fit.reason: Needed for credible flaring and methane reporting to partners and buyers, but it delivers value only once measurement programmes exist and the data infrastructure is in place.

entries.rationale: Strong refereed evidence that inventories under-count, but no direct quantified evidence that software itself cuts emissions, and no cost data.
entries.caveats: The benefit evidence shows the inventory gap, not software performance. No capex or opex source exists, since vendor pricing is not public. Kayrros, SLB, Honeywell and Validere are named from general knowledge. SensorUp and Qube claims are marketing and were not used as evidence. Alvarez and Sherwin figures come from abstracts or search summaries.
